principles: The CLI must mechanically surface progress instead of relying on host final-response discipline.
The appended output must be the actual milestone_status table users can already request manually.
JSON and read-only command contracts must remain stable.
Commands for stories without milestone ledgers should not gain noisy fabricated progress.
drivers: The user wants the consumed milestone table printed to stdout.
Multiple story-scoped commands can mutate checklist, evidence, phase, summary, delivery, or milestone ledger state.
Existing handlers have command-specific output contracts that tests may depend on.

options.name: Append table in each mutating handler
cons: Higher risk of missing future commands

options.name: Central CLI post-command renderer
pros: Single mechanical path for all configured commands
Preserves handler storage logic and makes stdout behavior testable at the CLI boundary
cons: Needs care to avoid JSON mode and read-only commands

rationale: A central post-command renderer best matches the desired consumption layer and avoids depending on each handler author to remember milestone progress output.

preMortem.scenario: The hook prints after JSON commands and corrupts machine-readable output.
preMortem.trigger: A command is run with --json or --format=json and the hook appends a human table.
preMortem.mitigation: Detect JSON-format invocations and skip the human post-command table for machine-readable modes.

preMortem.scenario: The hook fabricates progress for stories without milestone ledgers.
preMortem.trigger: A mutating command has a storyId but milestone_status would report missing ledger.
preMortem.consequence: Users see noisy or misleading progress output.
preMortem.mitigation: Only append when the status report indicates a present milestone ledger.

preMortem.scenario: A representative handler test passes but real CLI stdout does not include the table.
preMortem.trigger: Tests call handler functions directly instead of invoking the CLI command path.
preMortem.mitigation: Add a CLI-level regression that executes a state-changing command and asserts stdout contains the table headings.
